newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Formin laments peripatetic life.
newsitem.headline: Irish Formin laments peripatetic life.

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring lamented on Friday that his role as President of the EU's Council of Foreign Ministers meant spending little time at home in his native Tralee.

Spring, who reckons that he will travel 150,000 miles (241,000 km) by plane during Ireland's six-month EU presidency, said in a speech on the eve of an EU Foreign Ministers' session that he and his colleagues all missed their homes.
He quoted from a letter written by a British soldier to his parents during the first World War which said:
"Dear People. I am at present in Bethlehem, where Jesus Christ was born. I wish to Christ that I was in Wigan, where I was born."

"I can share that young soldier's sentiments, as indeed do my wife and family," said Spring, who pushed for the regular informal session of EU ministers to be held in Tralee, deep in the beautiful southern region of Kerry.
Spring is proud of his home region and tried to get U.S. President Bill Clinton to play golf at nearby Ballybunion during a visit to Ireland last November.

But the 18 holes were postponed for lack of time and residents are now hoping that Clinton will squeeze in a game on their beautiful course if he is reelected and makes a visit to Ireland in late November or December.
